Spaghetti plot of individual NPX trajectories

Source: R/plot_spaghetti.R
plot_spaghetti.Rd

Plots one line per subject across time (a "spaghetti" plot), optionally faceted by a grouping variable (e.g. treatment group) with an overlaid LOESS trend line. Mirrors the trajectory figures in the NUMAB reports.

Usage

plot_spaghetti(
  data,
  assay = NULL,
  subject_id = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  facet_by = NULL,
  assay_col = NULL,
  value_col = NULL,
  lod_col = NULL,
  show_lod = FALSE,
  smooth = "loess",
  alpha_line = 0.4,
  alpha_point = 0.5,
  palette = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  facet = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame in long format, or an OlinkExperiment.

assay

Name(s) of the protein/assay(s) to plot. If NULL, the first assay in `assay_col` is used. When multiple assays are supplied, the plot is faceted by assay.

subject_id

Name of the column identifying individual subjects. If NULL, auto-detected (e.g. "SubjectID", "Patient", "PPID").

time

Name of the column containing time points. If NULL, auto-detected (e.g. "Time", "Timepoint", "Visit").

group

Optional column name to color individual lines by.

facet_by, facet

Optional column name to facet the plot by (e.g. "TreatGroup").

assay_col

Name of the assay column. If NULL, auto-detected (e.g. "Assay").

value_col

Name of the NPX value column. If NULL, auto-detected (e.g. "NPX").

lod_col

Optional column name holding a per-assay LOD value; a dashed "MaxLOD" reference line is drawn at the maximum value per facet.

show_lod

Logical; if `TRUE`, auto-detects the LOD column and draws a dashed reference line (default `FALSE`).

smooth

Optional smoothing method for an overlaid trend line: "loess", "lm", "gam", or "none" (default "loess").

alpha_line

Alpha for individual lines (default 0.4).

alpha_point

Alpha for individual points (default 0.5).

palette

Optional color palette for `group`.

title

Plot title.

...

Additional arguments passed to `ggplot2::stat_smooth()`.

Value

A ggplot object.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
plot_spaghetti(
  bansal_longitudinal, assay = "HAGH",
  subject_id = "Assigned Participant  ID", time = "Time",
  facet_by = "Long_COVID status"
)
} # }
